concept.name: Initial balance
concept.definition: In Market Profile analysis (developed by J. Peter Steidlmayer at the Chicago Board of Trade in the 1980s), the price range established during the first hour of the regular trading session — the first two 30-minute TPO periods — taken to represent the range set by short-term, day-timeframe traders before longer-term participants extend it. It is an analytical convention within the Market Profile framework, not a proven predictive law.
concept.intuition: The first hour's high and low mark the territory day traders carve out; whether later trading holds or breaks that range tells you whether bigger money is participating.
concept.mechanics: On a Market Profile (TPO) chart, the session is divided into 30-minute periods labeled with letters; the initial balance is the price range covered by periods A and B of the regular session. Moves beyond the IB high or low are called range extensions and are used to gauge initiative buying or selling.
concept.formula: IB_high = max price traded during the first two 30-minute periods (first hour) of RTH; IB_low = min price over the same window; range extension = any trade beyond IB_high or IB_low in later periods.
concept.failure_modes: The one-hour convention fits the pit-era U.S. day session for which it was designed; in near-24-hour electronic markets the 'first hour' is a design choice, and IB-based rules lose meaning on days dominated by a single scheduled news event.
concept.misconceptions: The initial balance is not an official exchange statistic and has no universal definition across platforms (some use the first hour, others the first two TPO periods of a user-defined session); IB extensions describe structure, they do not predict direction with verified accuracy.
concept.example: If CBOT-era bond futures trade between 98-04 and 98-20 in the first hour, that band is the initial balance; a move above 98-20 in period C is an upside range extension attributed to longer-term buyers.

citations.source: WindoTrader Market Profile Glossary, Part 1: Market Profile Terminology
citations.section: Initial balance (IB): 'represents the first hour of trading... letters A and B together'
